app.title: Cloud2Grid Explorer (Streamlit)
app.summary: A person picks a recorded weather event and a model, then plays the event or scrubs through it one time step at a time. At each step, a satellite image with the plant locations, a network diagram coloured by line loading or by model error, and a timeline of solar output and grid import all move together, so the model can be checked against the physics reference. A guided tour walks through the same event as captioned slides. Other pages set every model stage against the reference: how strongly each input moves the import, per-stage metric bars and verdicts, and a counterfactual that prices the extra import caused by cloud at historical market prices.

task.text: Compare a learned grid model's predicted network states and sensitivities with a physics-based reference across recorded weather events and model training stages.

data.text: Precomputed bundles for a few weather events: satellite image frames every 15 minutes, satellite-derived solar output per plant, half-hourly simulated network states (bus voltages and branch flows) from a physics solver and from each model stage, per-stage summary metrics and regression slopes, and half-hourly market prices.
data.item: a time step of a weather event: one satellite frame with the network state held for that half-hour, under the reference and under each model

stage.text: comparing frozen model predictions against the physics reference after training, and presenting the comparison

mechanism.text: An event picker, a model switcher and a time slider or Play button drive three linked panels: a satellite image with plant overlays, a network diagram coloured by loading or error, and a timeline with a cursor. Separate pages put the model stages side by side as scatter panels, slope bars, metric bars and tables. A stepper turns the same event into a captioned guided tour.

field.text: evaluating a learned power-flow model against AC power flow in power systems engineering

workflow.name: replay recorded events and compare model predictions with a reference

steps.here: choose a hero event from a select box; the frozen bundle for that event (frames, solar output, network states) loads

steps.step: choose which model to compare against the reference
steps.here: a segmented control switches the grid shown between the AC reference and each model stage, and a second one colours branches by loading or by error against AC

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: Play or the time slider moves through 15-minute satellite frames; the satellite image, the network state held from the half-hour and the timeline cursor all update together
partial-residual scatter panels per model, a decomposition of one half-hour step's import change into PV, load and battery terms, and bars of each driver's slope against the AC slope

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: metric bars, a metrics table with bootstrap intervals and the pre-registered verdict for each model stage, each set against its reference value

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: a five-stage stepper ends in an observed-versus-clear-sky counterfactual: the extra import per half-hour times the market price, summed over the day and the season
a guided tour plays the event as captioned slides with Back, Next, Replay this scene and Auto-play; the numbers are filled into the captions from the bundle

distinctive: every panel is labelled with its provenance (observed, derived, simulated, predicted or hypothetical), so measured and modelled quantities are never mixed up
satellite frames are 15-minute but grid states are half-hourly; the last grid state is held between frames and labelled as held, never interpolated
models are judged on sensitivity (how much the import moves per MW of solar, load or battery) as well as on the absolute error of the state
a series of model training stages is compared against one physics reference on the same fixed set of states, with pre-registered pass or fail criteria
a counterfactual re-solve with only one plant changed separates the effect of cloud from everything else that changed at the same time
